intents.title: Tables (a table)
intents.desc: The tables of the database window 1 is logged in to (their names like <like>, from information_schema: SHOW takes no ? in a prepared statement), drawn as a table in decode_emacs. Run on database window 1's session; nothing is sent to Emacs.

sql.statement: select table_name from information_schema.tables where table_schema = database() and table_name like ? order by table_name

intents.notes: D-db-session. The answer is the relay's as it is ({columns, rows, num_rows}); a row is an array, so the column is taken by its index. like goes to the ? as a value (a prepared statement), never into the text.

intents.title: Changed files of one section (a book shaped on window 1)
intents.desc: The book of magit.changed-files' table (b in its decode_emacs: ~work/books/decode/magit.changed-files.json) made the temporary table t_in on database window 1, and its files of one section (unstaged by default) taken from it in the book's order. A table in decode_emacs, and the rows of a run_table (run from db.magit-section): the template magit_stage stages each.

params.name: book
params.doc: a book under ~work/books (without .json) with the columns section and path

params.name: section
params.doc: the section of the files taken (unstaged, untracked, staged ...)

sql.statement: select section, path from t_in where section = ? order by _n

intents.notes: D-db-session: an example of the flow -- an intent's answer made a table (decode_emacs), the table a book (b), the book shaped by a statement on window 1 (sql.load), the answer the rows of a run_table (result.book). The book's columns are text; _n is its order.
